teachingReview.heading: Use the correct sequence
teachingReview.body: For people over 3 months with strongly suspected or confirmed bacterial meningitis, NICE recommends intravenous dexamethasone. Give it with or before the first antibiotic if possible, but never hold antibiotics while waiting.
teachingReview.review: Timing partial; current NICEage>3months/indication not closed.

teachingReview.heading: Handle a delayed start
teachingReview.body: If dexamethasone is delayed less than 12 hours after antibiotics, NICE recommends giving it as soon as possible. After a longer delay, obtain infection specialist advice because benefit is less certain.

teachingReview.heading: Reassess after identification
teachingReview.body: NICE recommends continuing dexamethasone for pneumococcus or Haemophilus influenzae type b and stopping it for other identified organisms. When no organism is found, specialist judgment guides continuation.
teachingReview.review: Book pneumococcal-only pathway differs from retained NICEpneumococcus/Hib.

teachingReview.heading: Monitor short-term steroid effects
teachingReview.body: A short systemic corticosteroid course can still cause mood changes, insomnia, indigestion, and fluid retention. Higher doses can increase blood pressure and blood glucose. Review symptoms, blood pressure, glucose, and infection course during treatment rather than assuming that a brief course has no adverse effects.
teachingReview.review: Complete new body supported. Steroid body uses explicit short-term effects/monitoring, not long-term incidence. SUP body translates unnecessary prophylaxis discontinuation into indication review, not blanket stopping of indicatedPPI.

teachingReview.heading: Monitor the adjunct
teachingReview.body: Review hyperglycemia, gastrointestinal bleeding risk, mental status, infection course, and other corticosteroid effects. The meningitis use is off-label in the NICE guideline and should follow the institution's current protocol.
teachingReview.review: Class monitoring partial; whole GIbleeding/off-label/current protocol pending.

teachingReview.heading: Reduce ventilation time
teachingReview.body: Use noninvasive support when safe, multimodal sedation strategies, daily spontaneous awakening and breathing trials, and early mobility to accelerate liberation.

teachingReview.heading: Position and protect the airway
teachingReview.body: Elevate the head of bed when not contraindicated, manage secretions, assess swallowing, and remove unnecessary nasogastric and endotracheal tubes.

teachingReview.heading: Update oral care
teachingReview.body: Provide daily toothbrushing without routine chlorhexidine. The 2022 update found unclear VAP benefit and a possible mortality signal with chlorhexidine.

teachingReview.heading: Reassess stress-ulcer prophylaxis
teachingReview.body: Review the indication for stress-ulcer prophylaxis and discontinue it when it is unnecessary. This is an indication review, not an instruction to stop every proton pump inhibitor: confirm why the patient is receiving treatment before changing the plan.
teachingReview.review: Complete new body supported. Steroid body uses explicit short-term effects/monitoring, not long-term incidence. SUP body translates unnecessary prophylaxis discontinuation into indication review, not blanket stopping of indicatedPPI.

teachingReview.heading: Feed and maintain deliberately
teachingReview.body: Use early enteral rather than parenteral nutrition when safe. Change ventilator circuits only when visibly soiled or malfunctioning.

teachingReview.heading: Prevent nonventilator HAP too
teachingReview.body: Hand hygiene, mobility, oral care, dysphagia and aspiration assessment, pulmonary hygiene, vaccination, and stewardship extend prevention beyond the ICU.
